title: Flaky windows test: matching-host Ladybug launcher version assertion fails on an identical tree
description:
FLAKE CONFIRMED BY TREE IDENTITY, not by judgement. test/ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:84, "matching-host Ladybug package qualification > the published launcher reports the real compiled Lore version through synchronous redirected output", in lint/typecheck/test (windows-latest).

THREE MEASUREMENTS, THE SAME BYTES, BOTH OUTCOMES:

  #207 head  82bbf578  tree 46925743e10843d4b0b8d51bb9d05f041b3b9cc0  windows PASSED
  push/main  1f34f8a3  tree 46925743e10843d4b0b8d51bb9d05f041b3b9cc0  windows FAILED  (run 35545097732, attempt 1)
  push/main  1f34f8a3  tree 46925743e10843d4b0b8d51bb9d05f041b3b9cc0  windows PASSED  (run 35545097732, attempt 2)

Byte-identical trees roughly three minutes apart, then the SAME SHA passing on re-run with nothing changed. The promoted set was five .quest/tasks/*.json files and nothing else; the failing assertion concerns a compiled launcher reporting its version, which no tracker JSON can reach. Attempt 1 reported 3195 pass / 141 skip / 1 fail across 3337 tests in 105 files.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING NOISE. This job is one of the five required contexts on dev (require-ci-on-dev, ruleset 22838594), so a flake here blocks a merge into dev; and it reddened main's post-promotion push run, which is the run that carries the `main is fast-forward of dev` guard. The guard itself passed. But a reader who takes the run's CONCLUSION rather than its job list sees a failed promotion, which is exactly the two-reds-one-colour trap this repository's profile already warns about -- here arriving as one red BY DESIGN on the pull_request run and one red BY ACCIDENT on the push run, on the same SHA.

WHAT THE FAILURE PROBABLY IS, EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED. The failing test was reported at [2056.37ms]. The test compiles a real Windows binary at line 103 via packageCompileCommand with timeout: 120_000, then asserts expect(compile.exitCode).toBe(0) at line 109 before spawning the launcher. Two seconds is far too fast for a bun --compile to have run, so the likely shape is a FAST compile failure surfacing at line 109 rather than a timeout or an output race -- a transient temp-dir, antivirus, or file-lock condition on the windows runner would fit. THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS, not a reading of the error.

EVIDENCE LOST, AND HOW: I re-ran the failed job before extracting the assertion text, and GitHub REPLACES a job's log on re-run for the same job id. Attempt 1's expect() output is unrecoverable; only the summary lines captured beforehand survive. The operational rule this earns: CAPTURE THE FAILING LOG BEFORE RE-RUNNING, because the re-run is what destroys the thing that would diagnose it. Next occurrence should run `gh run view --job <id> --log-failed > <file>` first, and only then re-run.

Note the repo already carries flake machinery for a different windows condition: the test step retries on "error: EEXIST: file already exists, epoll_ctl" or exit 124, with --max-concurrency and --timeout reduced on the retry. Whatever this is, it is not that one -- it is not caught by that grep.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The failure mode is identified from a CAPTURED failing log, not inferred -- the next occurrence is logged to a file before any re-run
Whether the failure is the line-109 compile assertion or the launcher spawn is settled with evidence, closing the hypothesis in this record rather than restating it
The test is made deterministic, or its transient condition is detected and retried the way the existing epoll_ctl/exit-124 retry already handles its own case -- not simply re-run by hand
A flake in this job is distinguishable from a real failure without tree-diffing by hand, since it is a required context on dev and can redden a promotion push run
